assessments.support: Raw and post-QC Ns by diagnosis are fully reported for both ABIDE I (discovery) and ABIDE II (validation).
Age, sex and site counts (11 sites for ABIDE II validation) are reported.
Athena pipeline explicitly named and its processing steps described.
ASD/Asperger grouping per DSM-5 is stated, but the diagnostic-instrument source (e.g. ADOS/ADI-R) for ABIDE labels is not independently restated beyond referring to the ABIDE repository.
Motion (FD), age, sex and site are explicitly reported and modeled.
Motion scrubbing with an explicit >5%-removed exclusion rule; site included as a covariate in group-level statistics.
Cortico-cerebellar connectivity via linear regression against cerebellar PCs (95% variance), applied identically in discovery and validation.
FDR correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) applied across all 65 cortical ROI tests.

risk_of_bias.summary: Well-documented discovery (ABIDE I) and independent validation (ABIDE II) design with explicit motion-based QC thresholds, named preprocessing pipeline, site-covariate handling, and multiple-comparisons correction; main gap is the diagnosis-source instrument not being independently restated.

charting.title: Abnormal Cortico-Cerebellar Functional Connectivity in Autism Spectrum Disorder
charting.primary_focus: Group-difference cortico-cerebellar functional connectivity, discovery + validation
charting.primary_goal: Identify and validate cortical regions showing differential (cerebellar) functional connectivity between ASD and TD
charting.country_region: Multi-site (ABIDE I + 11 sites in ABIDE II validation)
charting.disorder_diagnosis: Autism Spectrum Disorder (including Asperger syndrome per DSM-5)
charting.gender_distribution: 241/276 males (ABIDE I ASD); 234/269 males (ABIDE II ASD)
charting.gender_distribution_controls: 348/432 males (ABIDE I TD); 208/316 males (ABIDE II TD)
charting.dataset_openly_available: ABIDE data available via the ABIDE Consortium website; no separate analysis code repository mentioned
charting.specific_features: Cortico-cerebellar connectivity: linear regression between each cortical ROI time series and cerebellar principal components (95% variance); 65 cortical ROIs tested
charting.feature_change_direction: Hypoconnectivity (underconnectivity): reduced cortico-cerebellar functional connectivity in ASD vs TD across five ROIs discovered in ABIDE I, 3 replicated in ABIDE II
charting.validation_methodology: Discovery analysis in ABIDE I, independent replication analysis in ABIDE II (same preprocessing/statistics); FDR correction across 65 tests
charting.summary_key_findings: ASD showed reduced cortico-cerebellar functional connectivity with five cortical ROIs in the ABIDE I discovery sample (N=708); three of the five (right fusiform gyrus, right superior temporal gyrus, left middle temporal gyrus) replicated in an independent ABIDE II validation sample (N=585, 11 sites), all FDR-corrected.
charting.features_associated_disorder: Right fusiform gyrus, right postcentral gyrus, right superior temporal gyrus, right middle temporal gyrus, left middle temporal gyrus (cortico-cerebellar connectivity)
charting.future_directions_recommended: Further studies to comprehensively examine ASD-related differences in cortico-cerebellar functional connectivity, addressing incomplete cerebellar coverage.
charting.reviewer_notes: Strength: independent discovery/validation design across ABIDE I and II with identical pipeline and site-covariate adjustment.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational) discovery + independent validation; ABIDE I discovery N=708 (432 TD, 276 ASD), ABIDE II validation N=585 (316 TD, 269 ASD, 11 sites).
narrative_row.methods: Athena-pipeline-preprocessed rs-fMRI; FD-based motion scrubbing with >5%-removed exclusion rule; cortico-cerebellar connectivity via linear regression of 65 cortical ROIs against cerebellar PCs, with site as a covariate; FDR correction across tests.
narrative_row.outcomes: Five ROIs showed reduced (hypo-) cortico-cerebellar connectivity in ASD in ABIDE I; three (right fusiform gyrus, right superior temporal gyrus, left middle temporal gyrus) replicated in the independent ABIDE II sample.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Incomplete cerebellar coverage in some individuals (particularly posterior cerebellum); diagnosis-source instrument not independently restated; no atlas-based parcellation named.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: A clean discovery/validation example using both ABIDE I and ABIDE II with transparent QC and site-covariate handling, illustrating cross-release replication of an associational finding.

kg_link.sites: 11 (ABIDE II validation); ABIDE I site count not restated in extracted text
kg_link.finding: ASD showed reduced cortico-cerebellar functional connectivity in five cortical ROIs discovered in ABIDE I; three (right fusiform gyrus p=0.047, right superior temporal gyrus p=0.002, left middle temporal gyrus p=0.025, all FDR-corrected) replicated in the independent ABIDE II sample.
